notes:
SCOPE DELIVERED
- UI (packages/client/src/ui/**): createUi(root, host): UiHandle plus the full contract in ui/types.ts (UiScreen, UiSlot, UiDebugInfo, UiSettings, UiWorldEntry, UiSnapshot, UiHost, UiHandle) exactly as specified by client-a. Screens: loading, title, worldSelect, worldCreate, playing HUD, pause, inventory, settings. HUD has health, hunger, crosshair and a 9-slot hotbar; inventory has 36 slots plus a 3x3 crafting grid (the 2x2 subset is the top-left cells, per INVENTORY.craftGrid2/craftGrid3) and a result slot; settings expose renderDistance, fov, sensitivity, volume and showDebug; the F3 debug overlay shows FPS, XYZ, facing, biome, chunk count, draw calls and quad/triangle counts. update(snapshot) is diff-based (textContent/class only, no re-render) so it is safe to call every frame. All DOM stays under the provided root, global listeners are removed in dispose(), and createUi touches neither three.js nor Worker.
- Keybinds handled in the UI and forwarded to host: E -> onToggleInventory, Esc -> onCloseScreen/onResume, F3 -> onChangeSetting('showDebug', ...), 1-9 -> onSelectHotbar. Key handling is ignored while an input/textarea/contenteditable is focused.
- Audio (packages/client/src/audio/index.ts): createAudio({ manifest, baseUrl, volume }): AudioHandle with play/setVolume/dispose. WAV buffers are fetched from baseUrl + manifest.files[name] (assets-gen output only). When AudioContext, fetch or the manifest is unavailable (Node, jsdom, headless before a user gesture) it returns a silent no-op handle. It never throws and never calls console.error/console.warn, which is asserted by unit tests, so the zero-console-error E2E condition is preserved. UI clicks, block break/place and footsteps are routed through host.onPlaySound.
- Unit tests: 30 passing (25 UI + 5 audio). packages/client/vitest.config.ts does not exist yet (client-a owns it), so the DOM test file starts with the // @vitest-environment jsdom pragma as instructed.

BENCH MEASUREMENTS (pnpm bench, exit 0, tests/bench/results/bench.json)

- chunkMeshAvgMs = 1.887 ms (BENCH budget 12, fail > 36) -> ok

Totals: chunkGen 75.449 ms, mesh 60.383 ms, simTick 40.110 ms. No metric exceeded its threshold, so warnings and failures are both empty and exit code is 0.

FIXTURE SUBSTITUTION (yes - recorded in bench.json meta.fixtureSubstitution)
- packages/world, packages/sim and packages/gameplay are still scaffolds, so the bench does not depend on them. tests/bench/src/fixtures/ contains deterministic stand-ins built only on core-types primitives: terrain.ts (3-octave value noise over hashU32/hash01, bedrock, dirt/grass/sand, caves, ores, water to SEA_LEVEL; FIXTURE_TERRAIN_VERSION = bench-terrain-1), tick.ts (fixed-step gravity/ground-collision entity loop at PERF.simTickHz; FIXTURE_TICK_VERSION = bench-tick-1). These numbers therefore measure representative work at BENCH.renderDistance, not the real world/sim implementations, and must be re-baselined once those packages land.
- Mesher fallback flag: TRUE. bench.json meta.mesher = { source: 'bench-fallback', version: 'bench-fallback-1', fallbackUsed: true, reason: '@voxelcraft/client does not export meshSection, createEmptyPadded, setPaddedBlock, fillPaddedLight, countVisibleFaces yet' }. tests/bench/src/clientMesher.ts dynamically imports @voxelcraft/client, validates the required exports and only falls back when they are missing, so the bench switches to the real mesher automatically once client-a exports meshSection/createEmptyPadded/setPaddedBlock/fillPaddedLight/countVisibleFaces/MESHER_VERSION. The fallback emits one quad per visible face with no greedy merging, so chunkMeshAvgMs is expected to change when the real mesher is wired in.

E2E (pnpm test:e2e, exit 0)
- 4 tests: 2 passed, 2 skipped. Fixed seed 1337, renderDistance 2 (PERF.e2eRenderDistance), canvas 640x360 (PERF.e2eCanvasWidth/Height) via buildTestUrl() in tests/e2e/src/harness.ts.
- CONSOLE ERROR ZERO: confirmed. Both passing tests collect console errors and pageerror events through collectPageErrors(page) and assert the joined list is empty; the default boot and the ?test=1 boot both produced zero console errors.
- Screenshots written under tests/e2e/test-results/ (playwright outputDir): boot.png, boot-test-mode.png, seeded-boot.png.
- SKIPPED AND WHY: 'hud is mounted under #ui-root' and the full break/place/save/reload persistence spec are gated with test.skip because apps/game does not provide the integration hooks yet. apps/game/index.html only has <div id="app"> (no #ui-root) and apps/game/src/main.ts is still the scaffold, so window.__vc (ready/state/getBlock/breakBlock/placeBlock/save/hash/errors) and the ?test=1&seed&rd&w&h handling do not exist. apps/game/** is client-a's owned path, so I did not modify it. tests/e2e/specs/persistence.spec.ts is fully written and type-checked and asserts the required loop (seeded boot -> breakBlock -> placeBlock -> save -> reload -> window.__vc.hash() equality and getBlock equality -> screenshot persistence-after-reload.png -> zero console errors before and after); it will start running with no further changes as soon as window.__vc exists. ui-hud.png and persistence-after-reload.png are therefore not produced yet.
- The pre-existing tests/e2e/vitest.config.ts (include: unit/**) vs playwright specs/ split is unchanged; the new unit test lives in tests/e2e/unit/harness.test.ts and the new spec in tests/e2e/specs/. The original boot.spec.ts test was kept and strengthened rather than replaced.

IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS WORTH FLAGGING
- UiSlot.durability is treated as a 0..1 remaining fraction used to size the durability bar; null means the item has no durability. The contract does not state the unit, so client-a should feed a normalized value (or tell me to switch to absolute values).
- worldSelect <-> worldCreate navigation is handled locally inside the UI (there is no UiHost callback for it); only onCreateWorld/onSelectWorld/onDeleteWorld reach the host. Escape clears that local override.
- data-testids present as specified (hud, crosshair, hotbar, hotbar-slot-0..8, health, hunger, debug-overlay, inventory-screen, crafting-grid, pause-screen, settings-screen, world-select, world-create) plus extra granular ids (debug-fps, debug-pos, inventory-slot-0..35, crafting-cell-0..8, crafting-result, setting-<key>, world-play-<id>, world-delete-<id>, ...) for precise assertions.

OTHER
